1.36 A receipt you can reuse

A useful result says: what was requested, which actual sources/owners were bound, what was submitted once, the genuine terminal, expected native changes, preserved records/bytes, independently observed outcome, closed resources, and remaining holds. A failed result belongs in the same chain.

Worker capture cleanup must preserve that chain on ordinary failures too. The CaptureFinalizer component seals used sessions, or asks their producers to prove a never-used branch, and saves both inventories before closing the caller-owned directory descriptors once. An incomplete attempt retains its session and original failure; it cannot be relabeled unused. Reporting failure after acknowledged closure is recorded separately from ownership uncertainty. The parent must still audit every helper before worker reap and reservation release. This component does not start or settle processes, publish previews, or authorize release. Its fault controls and disposable journal checks qualify cleanup ordering, not a production publisher. Keep the old worker disabled until its composed lifecycle and inherited-resource checks pass; undo a source-only integration by retaining the previous worker and its receipts, never replaying a failed publication.

Keep private run receipts locally. Public reports should replace user paths and catalog/cloud identifiers with role names and scoped counts. Publish your own source and synthetic controls; link primary documentation for supported product behavior. Do not redistribute decompiled proprietary bodies or signed credentials.

Status examples in this guide are qualified observations through 2026-10-12, not a claim that the entire catalog/cloud recovery is complete. Read the README for the current public implementation and release limits.
